# Temple Scroll Column 20 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 20 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**20:1** You shall place all these on the palms of Aaron and on the palms of his sons

**20:2** and wave them as an elevation offering before Me.

**20:3** Then you shall take them from their hands and turn them into smoke on the altar, upon the burnt offering,

**20:4** as a pleasing aroma before Me; it is an offering by fire to the LORD.

**20:5** You shall take the breast of the ram of ordination that belongs to Aaron and elevate it as an elevation offering before Me,

**20:6** and it shall be your portion.

**20:7** You shall consecrate the breast of the elevation offering and the thigh of the contribution

**20:8** that was elevated and that was set aside from the ram of ordination — from that which belongs to Aaron and from that which belongs to his sons.

**20:9** It shall be a perpetual due for Aaron and his sons from the children of Israel.

**20:10** You shall ordain them for seven days; each day offering a young bull as a sin offering for atonement.

**20:11** You shall purify the altar when you make atonement upon it, and you shall anoint it to consecrate it.

**20:12** For seven days you shall make atonement upon the altar and consecrate it,

**20:13** and the altar shall be most holy; whatever touches the altar shall become holy.

**20:14** This is what you shall offer upon the altar: two yearling lambs each day, perpetually.

**20:15** The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer at twilight.

**20:16** With a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter-hin of beaten oil; and a drink offering of a quarter-hin of wine for each lamb.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 20 is well preserved. It covers three interconnected topics: the completion of the ordination wave/elevation rite (20:1-9), the seven-day altar consecration (20:10-13), and the daily perpetual offering (20:14-16). "Elevation offering" (tenufah) — modern scholarship increasingly renders this as "elevation" rather than "wave," as the gesture was likely a vertical presentation before God. The transition to the tamid offering (20:14) establishes the permanent daily rhythm of the sanctuary. Parallels Exodus 29:24-42.*
